floor_history.headline: recon: floor=2 is pure sched1 lbu-emission-order swap in FALSE-color branch; regs+opcodes identical, only [b,r,g] vs [r,g,b]; statement-reorder KILLED
s2 structural: struct-cast, walking-pointer, ternary-hoist, block-local-split all KILLED at floor=2; two-block lbu structure is load-bearing (cannot consolidate)

s3 structural: named-intermediate rg, block-local cp, and function-scope cp all KILLED at floor=2 (function-scope cp regressed to 15); CSE/copy-prop collapse leaves sched1 dependence DAG untouched, ch
s4 permuter chassis-1 basin exhausted (~32k iters, ~24 min): best novel score=10 (loop1 boolean staged through existing `b` — dead-store cheat); every sub-40 basin form is variable-reuse / dead-store

frontier.hypothesis: A LIVE-code extension of `b`'s liveness across loop1 (not a dead per-iteration store) — e.g. accumulating an early-loaded copy of `*(u8*)(player+0x1A)` in `b` BEFORE loop1, then re-loading it in the FALSE arm as the same variable — perturbs FALSE-arm entry register pressure the same way the dead-store cheat does but with semantic purpose. Corroborated by the s4 permuter finding that the reuse-`b` axis moves sched1 (40->10).
frontier.mechanism: If `b` is set to the eventual color byte early (before loop1) as `b = *(u8*)(player+0x1A);` and consumed unchanged in the FALSE arm, b's live range spans the loops and cc1's register allocator may pin b to a callee-save distinct from the current build's choice at 0x15cc. The value is genuinely computed (used later); no dead store. Risk: cross-arm live b may cost a callee-save spill in the TRUE arm (which overwrites b via v = func_8004881C(b,g,r); return through gnd_load_tex(v<<16|v<<8|v)).
frontier.next_probe: Edit FALSE arm's prologue: hoist `b = *(u8*)(player+0x1A);` to BEFORE loop1 (top of function, after player NULL check). In FALSE arm, drop the `b = ...0x1A` re-assignment (b already holds it). In TRUE arm, keep `b = ...0x1A` (may need re-read since TRUE arm passes b as an arg then overwrites via v; check whether TRUE arm sandbox regresses). Sandbox --disable all. If FALSE-arm floor moves AND TRUE-arm doesn't regress, this axis has a legitimate spelling. If TRUE-arm regresses more than FALSE gains, need a variant that only extends b's liveness on the FALSE path (e.g. compute b twice — once early, once in FALSE arm — jumping into arm from a shared prologue).

frontier.hypothesis: Run cc1 -da with BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG + BB2_SCHED_DEBUG on both the s3 candidate AND the score-10 permuter form; compare .greg output at .L80041798 to identify EXACTLY which pseudo/hard-reg differs at FALSE-arm entry. That difference names the register-pressure lever a legitimate C form must reproduce.
frontier.mechanism: The score-10 form's byte-diff dropped from 2 to ~1 due to a specific pseudo landing in a different hard reg at 0x15cc. cc1's .greg dump lists Register dispositions per pseudo + conflict lists. Diffing the two dumps at the FALSE-arm block header will show the exact allocation delta the reuse-`b` axis induces.
frontier.next_probe: Bootstrap tmp/gccdbg/cc1 with BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 BB2_SCHED_DEBUG=1 (per register-alloc-pure-c doc). Preprocess src/text1a.c to two variants (s3 baseline + s4 loop1-boolean-stage form). Compile both with the instrumented cc1, capture .greg output. Diff `;; Register dispositions:` sections filtered to insns inside .L80041798 block. Identify which pseudo(s) moved between hard regs. Enumerate C constructs that would force that same allocation legitimately (arg-passing tweaks, param typing changes, structural liveness extensions of a semantically-used value).

frontier.hypothesis: An EARLIER load of one of the FALSE-arm color bytes into a live-across-call temporary — e.g. `s32 rr = *(u8*)((u8*)player + 0x18);` computed BEFORE the loops and consumed in BOTH arms (in FALSE as `r`, in TRUE arm as an arg to func_8004881C via `r` param) — is a live-code duplicated-read that perturbs pressure similarly. Aligns with [[duplicated-statement-into-arms]] and [[split-read-defeats-hoist]] SOTN-sanctioned families.
frontier.mechanism: Duplicating a color-byte load into both arms (rather than in each arm block-locally) extends r/g/b's live range across the loops. cc1's register allocator sees the value as live-across-loop and picks a callee-save differently than current build. Byte-neutrality: the load itself is real (unchanged bytes), just relocated. sanction applies if permuter shows byte-neutral form exists AND lever-exhaustion documented.
frontier.next_probe: Edit gnd_init_80041688 to hoist `s32 r0 = *(u8*)((u8*)player + 0x18);` (and/or g0/b0) BEFORE the p[1] flag pokes, then use r0 as the FALSE-arm's `r` (drop the re-load); in TRUE arm consume `func_8004881C(b, g, r0)` (or re-read the byte, testing which). Sandbox each of the 6 hoist combinations (r only / g only / b only / r+g / r+b / g+b) with --disable all. If any drops floor to 0 or below 2 with byte-neutral effect on TRUE arm, vet the closing form via cheat-reviewer (checking dead-store prong and duplicated-statement-into-arms prerequisites).
